# xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot (Data Source)

Fetches the Azure resources Xshield expects in one subscription and region, already rendered: a network security group of Xshield's own for each network interface or subnet it enforces at, with the group's whole rule set, and the association that puts each group there. Xshield places its group on a network interface or subnet that carries no group of yours, and Azure applies both. Where every network interface or subnet of a workload carries a group of yours, Xshield's rules for the workload go into your subnet's group instead, ahead of your rules and naming only the workload's own addresses, so your rules still decide the traffic of everything else the group covers. The groups and associations are keyed by `ct-policy-` and a hash of their network interface or subnet, which stays the same when a group's name comes from the subscription's name template, so a plan names the level each change is for.

Use it through the `azure` enforcement module, which creates these resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Most configurations use this through the azure enforcement module, which
# creates every resource it lists. Reading it directly is useful for review:
# what would the next apply hold, and where does each workload's group go?
# Without enforcement_plan, which only the module sets, such a read does not
# count as the pipeline's plan, so it cannot hide a pipeline that has stopped.
data "xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot" "this" {
  cloud_account_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  region           = "eastus2"
}

output "groups" {
  value = sort(keys(data.xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot.this.network_security_groups))
}

output "where_each_asset_is_enforced" {
  value = { for id, asset in data.xshield_azure_enforcement_snapshot.this.assets : id => asset.level }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the snapshot is for.
- `region` (String) Azure region the snapshot is for, by its name, such as `eastus2`.

### Optional

- `enforcement_plan` (Boolean) Set to `true` where this read is the enforcement workspace's plan, as the `azure` enforcement module sets it. Xshield then records the read as the pipeline's `last_checked_at`, and refuses it once the subscription is handed back to the cloud connector. Leave it unset for a read made to review the snapshot, so that the read cannot hide a stopped pipeline.
- `version` (String) The snapshot's version, which is the hash of everything it asks for. Set it to pin a version, for break-glass rollback or forensics. When omitted, the version Xshield expects is fetched, so the configuration never changes when policy does.

### Read-Only

- `assets` (Map of Object) Where each Xshield asset is enforced, keyed by Xshield asset ID. `level`: `networkInterface` or `subnet`. Null when the asset was refused, when its policy writes no rule, or when Xshield enforces it nowhere. `network_security_groups`: keys, in `network_security_groups`, of Xshield's groups that carry the asset's rules. `customer_network_security_groups`: keys, in `customer_network_security_groups`, of your groups that carry them. Both are empty when `level` is null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assets))
- `contained_interface_associations` (Map of Object) Associations of a workload Xshield's cloud connector contains, keyed by the group's key. The connector contains a workload by putting a network security group of its own on the network interface in place of Xshield's, and puts Xshield's back when the containment is reverted, so the `azure` enforcement module keeps each association in its state unchanged and creates none: either would take the connector's group off. An association no earlier apply made is left out until the containment is reverted. `level_id`: resource ID of the network interface. `network_security_group_id`: resource ID of the group the apply associated, as the state holds it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contained_interface_associations))
- `contained_subnet_associations` (Map of Object) As `contained_interface_associations`, for a subnet. `level_id`: resource ID of the subnet. `network_security_group_id`: resource ID of the group the apply associated. azurerm reads a subnet association's group back from the subnet, so the module gives a contained one the group the subnet carries now. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contained_subnet_associations))
- `customer_network_security_groups` (Map of Object) Each network security group of yours that takes Xshield's rules for workloads, because it is on the network interface or subnet each workload's enforcement scope names, keyed by `customer-nsg-` and a hash of its resource ID. `id`, `resource_group_name` and `name`: the group's resource ID, resource group and name. `security_rules`: Xshield's rules for the group, each naming only its workload's own addresses, with no allow of all traffic, as your rules decide the rest. Their `priority` gives only the order Azure is to evaluate them in: read them through `xshield_azure_security_rules`, which numbers them ahead of your rules. `subnets`: each subnet carrying the group whose workloads the rules are for, by resource ID, with the Xshield asset IDs of those workloads. `network_interfaces`: the same for each network interface carrying the group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_network_security_groups))
- `customer_network_security_groups_awaiting_room` (Map of Object) Each network security group of yours on which Xshield refused workloads because your rules leave too few priorities ahead of them, keyed as in `customer_network_security_groups`. `id`, `resource_group_name` and `name`: the group's resource ID, resource group and name. `priorities_wanted`: by direction, `Inbound` or `Outbound`, how many priorities ahead of your rules Xshield's rules for the group would take with the refused workloads'. Where your code declares the group's rules, `xshield_azure_security_rules` moves them up to make that room. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_network_security_groups_awaiting_room))
- `handover_interface_associations` (Map of Object) As `handover_subnet_associations`, for a network interface. `network_security_group`: key, in `network_security_groups`, of the group to associate. `network_interface_id`: resource ID of the network interface. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--handover_interface_associations))
- `handover_subnet_associations` (Map of Object) Associations of subnets the cloud connector enforced at with a group of its own while the subnet had none, keyed by the group's key. Azure takes an association by clearing whatever group its subnet carries, so creating one while the connector's group is on the subnet would leave it with no group until the apply ends. Once this version's groups are applied, the connector puts each one in place of its own group in a single change, and the `azure` enforcement module then takes the association over by importing it, so the subnet is never left without a group. Each moves to `subnet_associations` once an apply has taken it over. `network_security_group`: key, in `network_security_groups`, of the group to associate. `subnet_id`: resource ID of the subnet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--handover_subnet_associations))
- `held_interface_associations` (Map of Object) Associations an earlier apply made whose network interface now carries a network security group of yours in place of Xshield's, keyed by the group's key. Azure removes an association by taking whatever group its network interface carries off it, so removing one of these would remove your group. The `azure` enforcement module keeps each in its state unchanged while the network interface carries a group other than Xshield's, and Xshield drops it once the interface carries none. `level_id`: resource ID of the network interface. `network_security_group_id`: resource ID of the group the apply associated, as the state holds it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--held_interface_associations))
- `held_subnet_associations` (Map of Object) As `held_interface_associations`, for a subnet. `level_id`: resource ID of the subnet. `network_security_group_id`: resource ID of the group the apply associated. azurerm reads a subnet association's group back from the subnet, so the module gives a held one the group the subnet carries now. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--held_subnet_associations))
- `interface_associations` (Map of Object) Each network interface a group goes on, keyed by the group's key. `network_security_group`: key, in `network_security_groups`, of the group to associate. `network_interface_id`: resource ID of the network interface to associate it with. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interface_associations))
- `network_security_groups` (Map of Object) One network security group per network interface or subnet Xshield enforces at, keyed by `ct-policy-` and a hash of it. `name`: the key, or, when the subscription has a security group name template, the template's name for the group. A group keeps the name it was first applied under, so changing the template names only new groups. `resource_group_name`: resource group the group is created in, that of its network interface or subnet. `location`: region the group is created in. `tags`: `ct:delivery` and `ct:level`, which let the cloud connector recognise the group as Xshield's, never as one of yours. `security_rules`: the group's whole rule set. With the `azure` enforcement module's `enable_exclusive_rules` on, the default, it replaces any rule the group holds that it does not list; with it off, a rule not named as Xshield's stays alongside. Each rule has Azure's fields: `name`, `priority`, `direction`, `access` and `protocol`, and the source and destination as `source_address_prefix` or `source_address_prefixes`, `destination_address_prefix` or `destination_address_prefixes`, `source_port_range` or `source_port_ranges`, and `destination_port_range` or `destination_port_ranges`. A single value, which is how Azure takes `*` and a service tag, is in the singular field with the plural one empty; two or more are in the plural field with the singular one empty. Every rule set ends with an allow of all traffic in each direction at priority 4096, so traffic no Xshield rule decides passes as it did before the group, and lets the load balancer's health probes in at priority 100. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_security_groups))
- `published` (Boolean) False while Xshield has published nothing for this subscription and region, such as before the subscription is onboarded with policy delivery set to Terraform pipeline: every map is empty and `version` is null, so a configuration built on it plans no change. Only Xshield's own answer that nothing is published counts; any other failure to read the snapshot fails the plan.
- `released_interface_associations` (Map of String) Associations an earlier apply made that this version removes, keyed by the group's key, each with its network interface's resource ID. The `azure` enforcement module reads each network interface before it plans the removal, and fails the plan when the interface carries a group other than Xshield's, so a group of yours put there since Xshield last observed the subscription is never removed.
- `released_subnet_associations` (Map of String) As `released_interface_associations`, for a subnet, with the subnet's resource ID.
- `subnet_associations` (Map of Object) Each subnet a group goes on, keyed by the group's key. `network_security_group`: key, in `network_security_groups`, of the group to associate. `subnet_id`: resource ID of the subnet to associate it with. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subnet_associations))
